children: By Sarah Nassauer and Lauren Thomas
Wonder, a food delivery company started by Marc Lore, is exploring a sale of Grubhub, the delivery company it purchased in 2024, said people familiar with the matter.
Bankers have been in contact with Walmart, Target, Kroger and other retailers about a potential purchase, said the people. There are no guarantees a deal will come together.

Wonder sold Grubhub's college-campus meal-delivery unit to rival DoorDash for $300 million in September and said that DoorDash would also invest $125 million in Wonder. Wonder paid $150 million in cash and assumed $500 million of debt when it bought the company.
Wonder, which former Walmart executive Lore started in 2018, is laying the groundwork for a potential public offering and filed initial paperwork with regulators earlier this month.

Wonder originally focused on operating mobile kitchens from Mercedes Sprinter vans for home delivery. In recent years it has shifted focus to fixed locations that offer several restaurant food styles picked up or delivered from a single kitchen. It now has around 170 of such places. Lore has said he aims to build a mealtime "super app."

Grubhub's share of the meal-delivery business and its active users have fallen in recent years. DoorDash has purchased other competitors to grow quickly, and new entrants such as Walmart are also doing restaurant delivery.
Earlier this month, Amazon said it would end its partnership with Grubhub to offer the service free as part of its Prime membership bundle, instead swapping in a similar deal through Uber Eats.
The restaurant delivery space is in the midst of a period of consolidation. In October, DoorDash said it signed a deal to buy grocery-delivery company Instacart for $17 billion.
